source: Tenure types follow the FAO water tenure typology (FAO 2016, Exploring the concept of water tenure, Land and Water Discussion Paper 10; FAO 2020, Unpacking water tenure for improved food security and sustainable development; FAO 2024, Water tenure perspectives). Definitions are short paraphrases; consult the FAO publications for the authoritative wording. Use codes follow the water-use classification of the FAO water tenure assessment approach as applied in AlAfghani and Susetyo (2023). The analyzed flags and the type-level security ratings in this file are SYNTHETIC SAMPLE VALUES for the fictional Sample River Basin, not findings about any real place. Replace them with your own assessment's results, or set them to NA.

tenure_types.label: Land-based formal water right
tenure_types.definition: A formal right to use water that derives from land tenure (water follows the land) or from established prior use, typically exercised through an irrigation scheme's allocation rules.
examples: Scheme irrigation tied to land in the command area
Riparian use by landholders

tenure_types.label: Modern permit-based water right
tenure_types.definition: A long-term permit-based right to use water, separate from land, issued by the state and assertable against the state and third parties.
examples: Long-term abstraction permit
Entry in a water rights register

tenure_types.label: Regulatory licence
tenure_types.definition: A short-term (for example annual) licence to abstract or use water, renewed on a fixed cycle.
examples: Annual abstraction licence

tenure_types.label: Agency control
tenure_types.definition: Extensive legal powers granted to an irrigation, water or regional development agency or a utility to abstract, allocate and operate water resources.
examples: Basin agency operating a weir and its gates
Utility abstraction for public water supply

tenure_types.label: Water supply contract
tenure_types.definition: A written contract for the supply of water, for example bulk raw water from an agency to a utility or an industry.
examples: Bulk raw-water contract

tenure_types.label: Commonhold
tenure_types.definition: Rights to water held in common by a distinct community of users, such as the members of a water user organization. Check whether the organization exists in practice or only on paper.
examples: Registered water user association distributing a canal share

tenure_types.label: Investment contract
tenure_types.definition: Water rights or assurances embedded in an investment, concession or land-lease agreement.
examples: Plantation or industrial estate concession
Hydropower concession

tenure_types.label: De minimis / small-scale right
tenure_types.definition: The right to abstract and use small quantities of water for non-commercial purposes without administrative formalities (household use, garden plots, subsistence farming).
examples: Household dug well
Watering a garden plot from a stream

tenure_types.label: Exempt / declared commercial use
tenure_types.definition: Commercial water use that is exempted from permitting or only has to be declared.
examples: Small enterprise below a permit threshold

tenure_types.label: Reserve / minimum flow
tenure_types.definition: Water set aside by law or plan for the environment or for basic human needs.
examples: Environmental flow release below a weir

tenure_types.label: Other formal arrangement
tenure_types.definition: A formal water tenure arrangement not covered by the types above. Name the sub-type in the record description.

tenure_types.label: Customary tenure
tenure_types.definition: Rights and duties based on customary or local law, which formal law may or may not recognize; often tied to ancestral rules, customary office-holders or sacred sources.
examples: Spring governed by a customary steward
Rotation set by a ritual calendar

tenure_types.label: Religious-law tenure
tenure_types.definition: Water rights and duties derived from religious law or principles.
examples: Endowed well open to travellers

tenure_types.label: Informal tenure
tenure_types.definition: Water use that is not legally recognized, either illegal but tolerated by the water administration (sometimes for years) or simply illegal. Describe the practice neutrally and attribute any label of illegality to its source.
examples: Pumping from a canal without a permit
Unauthorized pipe or breach in a canal bank

tenure_types.label: Assumed tenure
tenure_types.definition: Formal water rights that are wrongly assumed to exist because of the official character of the user, typically a public or quasi-public body abstracting without a current instrument.
examples: Village water supply abstracting with an expired permit

tenure_types.label: Impossible tenure
tenure_types.definition: Formal rights are legally impossible because the presumed holder lacks legal capacity, for example an unregistered water committee or pump group.
examples: Unregistered community water committee
Informal farmer pump group

tenure_types.label: Unrecognised tenure
tenure_types.definition: Water-dependent livelihoods, such as inland fisheries or the use of wetland resources, that water law does not usually regulate at all.
examples: Fishing in a reservoir
Reed harvesting in a wetland

tenure_types.label: Other informal arrangement
tenure_types.definition: An informal water tenure arrangement not covered by the types above. Name the sub-type in the record description.

tenure_types.label: Unclassified
tenure_types.definition: The evidence does not yet allow a classification. The record should say what evidence would decide it.

use_types.label: H2 Recreation / landscape, other (incl. ritual and cultural sites)
